datasets.name: AdvBench
datasets.description: AdvBench accompanies the Greedy Coordinate Gradient attack paper on aligned large language models (LLMs). It lists harmful behaviors and harmful strings used to test adversarial suffixes.
datasets.caveats: Many behaviors are near duplicates, so later papers often use a filtered subset. Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: AgentDojo
datasets.description: AgentDojo is a dynamic environment for testing prompt injection against large language model (LLM) agents. It has 97 realistic user tasks and 629 security test cases.
datasets.dataType: Python environment with tasks, tools, and attacks
datasets.caveats: Running the benchmark calls commercial model interfaces and can incur usage costs. Results depend on the agent scaffold and the defenses that are enabled.

datasets.name: AgentHarm
datasets.description: The UK AI Security Institute and Gray Swan released AgentHarm to measure harmful behavior by large language model (LLM) agents. It covers 110 malicious agent tasks across 11 harm categories including fraud and cybercrime.
datasets.dataType: Agent tasks with synthetic tools and grading rubrics
datasets.caveats: The authors ask users not to train models on the benchmark. Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: AI Incident Database
datasets.description: The Responsible AI Collaborative catalogs real world incidents in which artificial intelligence (AI) systems caused or nearly caused harm. Weekly snapshots of the full database are available as downloadable archives.
datasets.dataType: Incident reports in JSON, CSV, and MongoDB dumps
datasets.caveats: Entries depend on media reports and on the work of volunteer editors. Coverage and classification can be uneven across regions and harm types.

datasets.name: AI Vulnerability Database (AVID)
datasets.description: The AI Vulnerability Database (AVID) records failure modes and vulnerabilities of machine learning models. Its GitHub repository stores reports and vulnerability entries in structured files.
datasets.caveats: The repository shows limited recent activity compared with active incident trackers. Check entry dates before relying on the database for current coverage.

datasets.name: BIPIA
datasets.description: Microsoft built the Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks (BIPIA) on large language models (LLMs). Tasks cover email, web, and table question answering, summarization, and code.
datasets.dataType: Task contexts, attack instructions, and evaluation code
datasets.caveats: The repository was archived in September 2026 and is now read only. Web and summarization data must be fetched from original sources.

datasets.name: Cybench
datasets.description: Cybench evaluates language model agents on 40 professional capture the flag (CTF) tasks from four competitions. Many tasks include subtasks that break the challenge into steps for finer scoring.
datasets.dataType: Task containers, subtasks, and agent harness
datasets.caveats: Tasks run vulnerable services inside containers on the host machine. Use an isolated environment and review model outputs before execution.

datasets.name: CyberBench (JPMorgan Chase)
datasets.description: CyberBench groups ten datasets to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on cybersecurity language tasks. Tasks include entity recognition, summarization, multiple choice, and text classification.
datasets.dataType: Scripts that assemble a unified CSV from source datasets
datasets.caveats: The repository was archived in May 2026 and is now read only. Source datasets keep their own licenses, which you must check separately.

datasets.name: deepset Prompt Injections
datasets.description: deepset published a labeled set of benign and prompt injection inputs for training detection classifiers. It includes English and German examples split into training and test sets.
datasets.caveats: The set is small and many injections are simple and easy to detect. Test detectors on harder benchmarks before using them in deployed systems.

datasets.name: Gandalf Ignore Instructions
datasets.description: Lakera released prompt injection attempts collected from its Gandalf password game. The prompts try to make a model ignore its instructions and reveal a secret.
datasets.caveats: All samples are attacks, so pair them with benign prompts for classifier training. Some prompts may include offensive language written by game players.

datasets.name: HarmBench
datasets.description: HarmBench is a standardized framework for evaluating automated red teaming of large language models (LLMs). The authors compared 18 red teaming methods against 33 target models and defenses.
datasets.dataType: Harmful behavior prompts, classifier, and evaluation code
datasets.caveats: Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: In-the-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
datasets.description: This dataset collects 15,140 prompts shared on Reddit, Discord, websites, and open datasets. Of these, 1,405 are jailbreak prompts aimed at large language models (LLMs).
datasets.dataType: Prompt text with platform and date metadata
datasets.caveats: Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: InjecAgent
datasets.description: InjecAgent benchmarks indirect prompt injection against tool integrated large language model (LLM) agents. It contains 1,054 test cases with 17 user tools and 62 attacker tools.
datasets.dataType: JSON test cases and evaluation code
datasets.caveats: Tool responses are simulated rather than executed in real applications. Real deployments with live tools may behave differently from these results.

datasets.name: InterCode-CTF
datasets.description: InterCode is a framework for interactive coding with execution feedback. Its capture the flag (CTF) split uses picoCTF problems solved inside a Bash environment.
datasets.caveats: Recent models solve most tasks, so the split now shows ceiling effects. Pair it with harder benchmarks such as Cybench or NYU CTF Bench.

datasets.name: JailbreakBench
datasets.description: JailbreakBench is an open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking large language models (LLMs). It pairs 100 harmful behaviors with 100 benign behaviors and a public leaderboard.
datasets.dataType: Behavior prompts, jailbreak artifacts, and evaluation library
datasets.caveats: Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: NYU CTF Bench
datasets.description: NYU CTF Bench provides dockerized capture the flag (CTF) challenges from CSAW competitions for testing language model agents. Categories include web, pwn, forensics, reverse engineering, crypto, and misc.
datasets.caveats: Challenges contain exploitable services that could be misused if exposed. Run them only in isolated containers on a controlled network.

datasets.name: RobustBench
datasets.description: RobustBench is a standardized benchmark and model zoo for adversarial robustness of image classifiers. It tracks certified and empirical robustness on CIFAR and ImageNet.
datasets.dataType: Pretrained models, leaderboard entries, and evaluation code
datasets.caveats: The benchmark covers image classifiers, not large language models or text systems. Pretrained model licenses vary by entry, so check each before reuse.

datasets.name: SecBench
datasets.description: SecBench evaluates large language models (LLMs) on cybersecurity with questions in Chinese and English. It spans nine subdomains such as data, network, application, and cloud security.
datasets.dataType: Multiple choice and short answer questions (JSONL)
datasets.size: 3,000 public questions from a pool of 47,910
datasets.caveats: Only a subset of the full question pool is public. The repository states no license, so confirm reuse terms with the authors.

datasets.name: SecQA
datasets.description: SecQA is a small multiple choice benchmark on computer security concepts for large language models (LLMs). GPT-4 generated the questions using content from a computer security textbook.
datasets.caveats: The set is small and machine generated, which limits statistical power. Treat scores as a quick check rather than a full evaluation.

datasets.name: Tensor Trust
datasets.description: Tensor Trust is an online game where players attack and defend large language model (LLM) prompts. The dataset contains over 126,000 prompt injection attacks and 46,000 defenses.
datasets.dataType: Attack and defense prompts with benchmark splits
datasets.caveats: The repository states no license, so confirm reuse terms with the authors. Player-written prompts may contain offensive content, so screen samples before sharing them.

datasets.name: WildJailbreak
datasets.description: The Allen Institute for AI built WildJailbreak from jailbreak tactics mined from real chatbot interactions. It holds 262,000 vanilla and adversarial prompt and response pairs.
datasets.dataType: Prompt and response pairs with harmful and benign labels
datasets.caveats: Access requires a Hugging Face account and acceptance of the dataset terms. Prompts contain harmful requests by design and may produce dangerous model outputs. Store them securely and follow the license and responsible use terms.

datasets.name: WMDP
datasets.description: The Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy (WMDP) benchmark measures hazardous knowledge in language models. It has 3,668 multiple choice questions on biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security.
datasets.caveats: Questions were filtered by experts to exclude sensitive and hazardous details. Use the set only for evaluation and unlearning research as the authors intend.

datasets.name: Awesome Cybersecurity Datasets (shramos)
datasets.description: This GitHub list gathers links to public cybersecurity datasets by topic. Topics include network traffic, malware, phishing, spam, fraud, and other areas.
datasets.caveats: The list was last updated in 2024 and some links may be broken. Verify each dataset at its original source before citing or using it.

datasets.name: Awesome Machine Learning for Cyber Security (jivoi)
datasets.description: This GitHub list collects datasets, papers, and tools for machine learning in cybersecurity. Sections cover phishing, spam, malware, network intrusion, fraud, and related topics.
datasets.caveats: The list is not updated often and some entries are outdated. Many dataset links are older and may no longer be available.

datasets.name: Awesome-LM-SSP
datasets.subcategory: AI safety, security, and privacy reading list
datasets.description: Awesome-LM-SSP is a curated list of papers and resources on safety, security, and privacy of large models. It also includes separate sections for benchmarks, toolkits, and public leaderboards.
datasets.caveats: The list focuses on research papers rather than on released datasets. Follow each listed paper to find its data release and license.

datasets.name: Cambridge Cybercrime Centre Datasets
datasets.description: The Cambridge Cybercrime Centre shares cybercrime datasets with academic researchers under legal agreements. Holdings include underground forums, phishing, advance fee fraud, spam, and scam URLs.
datasets.dataType: Forum posts, emails, URLs, and chat messages
datasets.caveats: Your institution must sign the data sharing agreement before any access is granted. Commercial use of the data is significantly restricted under the agreement terms.

datasets.name: IMPACT Cyber Trust
datasets.description: IMPACT offers cybersecurity datasets and tools from multiple providers at no cost. Eligible researchers sign one memorandum of agreement with the coordinating center.
datasets.dataType: Network, DNS, routing, and attack datasets
datasets.license: Memorandum of agreement per dataset class
datasets.caveats: Eligibility is limited to researchers in the United States and listed partner countries. Some datasets are restricted and require extra review before release.

datasets.name: Kaggle Cybersecurity Datasets
datasets.description: Kaggle hosts many community uploaded cybersecurity datasets that are searchable by keyword and tag. Official competition data such as IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection also appears in the index.
datasets.caveats: Many uploads are mirrors without clear provenance or license information. Prefer datasets posted by the original authors or their organizations.

datasets.name: SecRepo
datasets.description: SecRepo is a curated list of security data samples maintained by Mike Sconzo. It covers network, malware, system, and threat intelligence data from many sources.
datasets.license: CC BY 4.0 for hosted data, exceptions noted
datasets.caveats: Many links point to third party sites that may change or disappear. Check each source for current availability, documentation, and license terms.

datasets.name: Stratosphere Laboratory Datasets
datasets.description: The Stratosphere Laboratory at Czech Technical University hosts malware, normal, and mixed network captures. Collections include CTU-13, IoT-23, Hornet, and the Android Mischief dataset.
datasets.dataType: Packet captures and bidirectional flow files
datasets.caveats: Some captures contain live malware traffic and embedded malicious payloads. Analyze packet captures only on isolated systems without network access.

datasets.name: UNB Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC) Datasets
datasets.description: The University of New Brunswick Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC) lists its public research datasets. Topics include intrusion detection, malware, Internet of Things, DNS, URLs, and language models.
datasets.dataType: Index of datasets with download forms
datasets.license: Redistribution allowed with citation of dataset and paper
datasets.caveats: Each download passes through a short form that collects basic user details. Several older datasets have known labeling issues reported in the literature.

datasets.name: Zenodo Communities
datasets.description: Zenodo is a CERN research repository that hosts many security datasets with persistent identifiers. Communities group related records so users can browse collections by topic.
datasets.caveats: Quality and documentation vary widely by uploader and by community. Check the linked paper and license for each record before use.

datasets.name: ASVspoof 2019
datasets.description: The Automatic Speaker Verification Spoofing (ASVspoof) 2019 database covers synthesized, converted, and replayed speech. It includes logical access and physical access scenarios with separate protocols.
datasets.caveats: The speech is studio quality and comes from about 100 speakers. Models trained on it may not generalize to real world recordings.

datasets.name: ASVspoof 2021
datasets.description: The Automatic Speaker Verification Spoofing (ASVspoof) 2021 challenge added telephony channels and a speech deepfake task. Evaluation data for logical access, physical access, and deepfake tasks is hosted on Zenodo.
datasets.size: Logical access evaluation set about 7.8 GB
datasets.caveats: Training data comes from the ASVspoof 2019 release rather than a new set. Download both releases to run complete training and evaluation experiments.

datasets.name: ASVspoof 5
datasets.description: The Automatic Speaker Verification Spoofing (ASVspoof) 5 database uses crowdsourced speech from about 2,000 speakers. It includes spoofing attacks from 32 algorithms plus seven adversarial attacks.
datasets.caveats: The archives are large and need substantial storage and bandwidth. Use the official protocols to keep speaker partitions disjoint across splits.

datasets.name: Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC)
datasets.description: Meta released the Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC) dataset of face swap videos made with paid actors. The full set has over 100,000 clips from 3,426 actors.
datasets.caveats: Download requires an AWS account and acceptance of the data terms. The full set is very large and needs substantial storage and bandwidth.

datasets.name: FaceForensics++
datasets.description: FaceForensics++ contains 1,000 original videos and their manipulated versions from four face manipulation methods. It also includes the Google DeepFakeDetection subset with paid actors.
datasets.dataType: Video sequences, masks, and model files
datasets.caveats: Access requires a Google form and acceptance of the terms of use. Source videos were downloaded from YouTube, so respect the platform terms of use.

datasets.name: FakeAVCeleb
datasets.description: FakeAVCeleb pairs deepfake videos with cloned audio for multimodal detection research. It contains 500 real videos and 19,500 fake videos with matching audio.
datasets.caveats: Access requires a Google form and approval by the authors. Subjects are celebrities who did not consent to the manipulation of their likeness.

datasets.name: In-the-Wild Audio Deepfake
datasets.description: This dataset holds real and deepfake audio of 58 politicians and public figures collected online. It tests whether audio deepfake detectors generalize to realistic recordings.
datasets.license: Apache 2.0 per project page, CC BY-SA 4.0 per Hugging Face card
datasets.caveats: Clips depict real public figures, so handle them with care in publications. Do not use these recordings to train voice cloning or impersonation systems.

datasets.name: WaveFake
datasets.description: WaveFake contains about 175 hours of synthesized speech from several neural vocoder architectures. It supports research on detecting audio produced by neural speech synthesis systems.
datasets.dataType: Audio (WAV) generated from LJSpeech and JSUT
datasets.caveats: Fake audio comes from only two source speakers in English and Japanese. Detectors may learn speaker traits instead of the artifacts of synthesis.

datasets.name: Bank Account Fraud (BAF) Dataset Suite
datasets.description: Feedzai released six synthetic bank account opening datasets for the Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2022 conference. The suite supports research on fairness, class imbalance, and changing data distributions.
datasets.size: Six datasets of one million rows each, about 1.4 GB
datasets.caveats: The data is generated from a real dataset with privacy controls. Protected attributes such as age are included to support bias studies.

datasets.name: Credit Card Fraud Detection (ULB)
datasets.description: The Machine Learning Group at Universite Libre de Bruxelles (ULB) released European card transactions from two days. Only 492 of the 284,807 transactions are fraudulent, giving a highly imbalanced task.
datasets.dataType: Tabular features from principal component analysis, plus time and amount
datasets.license: Open Database License (ODbL) with Database Contents License
datasets.caveats: Most features are anonymized components, so feature engineering is limited. Severe class imbalance requires precision and recall metrics instead of plain accuracy.

datasets.name: DGraphFin
datasets.description: DGraphFin is a dynamic social graph from the Finvolution Group for graph anomaly detection. It has about 3 million nodes, 4 million dynamic edges, and 1 million labeled nodes.
datasets.dataType: Dynamic graph with node features and labels
datasets.caveats: The DGraph website (dgraph.xinye.com), the only download source, no longer resolved on 2026-10-25; confirm the data is available before planning a project around it. The download required a free account. Node features are anonymized, which limits interpretation of model results.

datasets.name: Elliptic Data Set
datasets.description: Elliptic released a Bitcoin transaction graph with 203,769 nodes and 234,355 edges. About 2 percent of transactions are labeled illicit and 21 percent licit.
datasets.dataType: Graph edge list and node features with labels (CSV)
datasets.caveats: Most nodes are unlabeled, so semi-supervised methods are common with this graph. The license forbids commercial use and redistribution of derivative versions.

datasets.name: Elliptic++
datasets.description: Elliptic++ extends the Elliptic dataset with 822,942 Bitcoin wallet addresses and their interactions. It supports detection of both illicit transactions and illicit actors.
datasets.dataType: Transaction and wallet graphs with features (CSV)
datasets.caveats: The files are hosted on Google Drive through a repository link. No license is stated in the repository, so confirm terms with the authors.

datasets.name: Elliptic2
datasets.description: Elliptic2 provides 122,000 labeled subgraphs of Bitcoin clusters inside a background graph. The background graph holds 49 million node clusters and 196 million edges.
datasets.caveats: The dataset is very large and needs substantial storage and memory. The license does not allow commercial use or redistribution of derivatives.

datasets.name: Fraud Dataset Benchmark (FDB)
datasets.description: Amazon Science compiled the Fraud Dataset Benchmark (FDB) from nine public fraud related datasets. Its Python loaders give standard train and test splits and metrics.
datasets.license: MIT (code), source datasets keep their own licenses
datasets.caveats: Loaders pull data from Kaggle, so you need a Kaggle account and competition access. The repository has not been updated since 2023, so some loaders may break.

datasets.name: IBM Transactions for Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
datasets.description: IBM researchers generated synthetic financial transactions with labeled laundering patterns for anti-money laundering (AML) research. Several dataset sizes and illicit ratios are available for different experiments.
datasets.caveats: The data is synthetic and the laundering typologies are predefined. Validate any findings on real transaction data where access is possible.

datasets.name: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection
datasets.description: Vesta Corporation and the IEEE Computational Intelligence Society (IEEE-CIS) released this Kaggle competition dataset. It contains e-commerce transactions with identity features and fraud labels.
datasets.caveats: You must join the competition on Kaggle before the data can be downloaded. Many feature names are masked, which limits interpretation of model behavior.

datasets.name: PaySim
datasets.description: PaySim is a synthetic mobile money dataset generated by an agent-based simulator. The simulator was calibrated on real transaction logs from an African mobile money service.
datasets.caveats: The data is simulated and fraud patterns follow simulator rules. Models may learn simulator artifacts that do not appear in real transactions.

datasets.name: AIT Log Data Set V2.0
datasets.description: The Austrian Institute of Technology (AIT) Log Data Set V2.0 covers eight simulated enterprise testbeds. Each testbed logs several days of benign activity followed by multi-step attacks.
datasets.dataType: Apache, auth, DNS, VPN, audit, Suricata, and system logs, PCAP files
datasets.caveats: Benign activity is simulated by scripts and may lack real user variety. The noncommercial license bars use of the data in commercial products.

datasets.name: ATLAS
datasets.description: ATLAS provides audit logs from multi-stage advanced persistent threat (APT) attacks on Windows hosts. Logs include Windows security events, Domain Name System (DNS) records, and browser activity.
datasets.dataType: Windows security, DNS, and Firefox logs
datasets.caveats: Attacks were staged in a small lab with limited benign noise. The paper appeared at USENIX Security 2021 without a DOI.

datasets.name: ATLASv2
datasets.description: ATLASv2 extends ATLAS with Sysmon and VMware Carbon Black Cloud logs. Researchers worked on the hosts for four days before running ten attack scenarios.
datasets.dataType: Sysmon, Carbon Black, Windows security, DNS, and Firefox logs
datasets.caveats: The hosts ran Windows 7, which is out of support. Many attack steps overlap across the ten scenarios, which reduces scenario diversity.

datasets.name: Atomic Red Team
datasets.description: Atomic Red Team is a library of small attack tests mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Teams run the tests to produce their own host telemetry.
datasets.caveats: This is a data generator and not a dataset of recorded logs. Tests change real systems and should run only in isolated lab machines.

datasets.name: BETH Dataset
datasets.description: The Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) extended tracking honeypot (BETH) dataset records kernel process calls from cloud honeypots. It also includes Domain Name System (DNS) logs, and each host shows at most one attack.
datasets.dataType: Kernel process logs and DNS logs (CSV)
datasets.size: More than 8 million events from 23 hosts
datasets.caveats: Download requires a free Kaggle account and acceptance of the dataset terms. Honeypot activity differs from the behavior of normal enterprise hosts.

datasets.name: CERT Insider Threat Test Dataset
datasets.description: The Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) CERT Division built synthetic logs of employee activity with injected insider threat scenarios. Files cover logons, devices, web, email, files, and personality scores.
datasets.size: Multiple releases from r1 to r6.2
datasets.caveats: All data is synthetic, and malicious insiders are very rare in each release. Release r6.2 has five malicious insiders among about 4,000 simulated users.

datasets.name: DARPA Transparent Computing (Engagements 3 and 5)
datasets.description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Transparent Computing program recorded system provenance during red team exercises. Advanced persistent threat (APT) attacks ran against continuous benign activity.
datasets.dataType: Provenance records in Common Data Model (CDM) Avro format
datasets.caveats: Data sits on Google Drive and needs large storage and custom parsers. Ground truth is in prose reports rather than labeled events.

datasets.name: EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES
datasets.description: This collection holds Windows event log (EVTX) files that capture specific attack techniques. Folders follow MITRE ATT&CK tactics to support detection testing and threat hunting.
datasets.caveats: Samples are short and isolated, so they lack benign baseline activity. The repository has not received new samples or updates since 2023.

datasets.name: HDFS Console Logs (SOSP 2009)
datasets.description: This dataset holds Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) logs from a benchmark workload with block-level anomaly labels. It is a standard benchmark for log-based anomaly detection research.
datasets.dataType: Raw logs and labeled message count vectors
datasets.caveats: Anomalies reflect system faults and performance problems rather than security attacks. Recent studies show simple methods reach near-perfect scores on it.

datasets.name: KYPO Cybersecurity Training Shell Commands
datasets.description: This Masaryk University dataset records shell commands typed by trainees in KYPO cyber range exercises. Each training folder includes command logs, metadata, and the sandbox definition used.
datasets.caveats: The dataset is small and reflects student learners rather than attackers. It captures typed commands only and does not include full host telemetry.

datasets.name: LANL User-Computer Authentication Associations in Time
datasets.description: This LANL dataset records successful user-to-computer authentication events across an enterprise network. It supports graph and anomaly detection research on enterprise credential use.
datasets.caveats: The data has no attack labels, so it suits unsupervised research. Each record has only time, user, and computer fields and no other context.

datasets.name: LID-DS
datasets.description: The Leipzig Intrusion Detection Data Set (LID-DS) records system calls from services under normal use and attack. Attack scenarios exploit real published vulnerabilities in containerized server applications and services.
datasets.dataType: System call traces with arguments and network captures
datasets.caveats: Downloads are hosted on Proton Drive rather than the repository. Scenarios run in containers and may not match full host behavior.

datasets.name: Loghub
datasets.description: Loghub is a collection of system logs from distributed systems, supercomputers, operating systems, and applications. Several logs carry anomaly labels that support log analytics and detection research.
datasets.caveats: Only some datasets in the collection have anomaly labels for evaluation. Most logs describe system failures and faults rather than security attacks.

datasets.name: Loghub-2.0
datasets.description: Loghub-2.0 provides large annotated log datasets for evaluating log parsing methods. It covers 14 systems with template labels for each line.
datasets.size: About 3.6 million annotated lines per dataset on average
datasets.caveats: Annotations target log template extraction and not anomaly or attack detection.

datasets.name: Microsoft GUIDE
datasets.description: GUIDE is a Microsoft dataset of real security incidents with analyst triage labels. It spans alerts and evidence from more than 6,100 organizations.
datasets.size: About 13 million evidence rows, 1.6 million alerts, 1 million incidents
datasets.caveats: Identifiers are scrubbed, so raw log content is not available. Download requires a free Kaggle account and acceptance of the dataset terms.

datasets.name: OTRF Security-Datasets (formerly Mordor)
datasets.description: The Open Threat Research Forge (OTRF) Security-Datasets project shares logs from simulated adversary techniques. Datasets map to MITRE ATT&CK and include Windows events, Sysmon, and network captures.
datasets.dataType: Windows event logs, Sysmon logs, PCAP files (JSON)
datasets.caveats: Most datasets capture short attack runs with little benign background activity. Repository activity has slowed, with no new commits since early 2024.

datasets.name: Splunk Attack Data
datasets.description: Splunk Attack Data is a curated set of logs from simulated attacks mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. It supports detection rule development and testing for Splunk security content.
datasets.dataType: Sysmon, Windows Security, EDR, and AWS logs
datasets.caveats: Files are stored with Git Large File Storage (LFS), so plain clones miss data. Each file covers a narrow technique with little benign context.

datasets.name: Splunk Boss of the SOC v1 (BOTSv1)
datasets.description: Boss of the Security Operations Center (BOTS) v1 is a Splunk capture-the-flag (CTF) dataset. It combines Windows, Sysmon, firewall, intrusion detection, and network stream data from staged incidents.
datasets.caveats: Full use requires a Splunk installation and the matching technology add-ons. Challenge questions and answers sit in a separate Splunk scoreboard repository. The data may contain profanity or offensive language kept from the scenarios.

datasets.name: Splunk Boss of the SOC v2 (BOTSv2)
datasets.description: BOTSv2 is a Splunk capture-the-flag (CTF) dataset with more than 90 source types. It covers Windows, Linux, Active Directory, firewalls, endpoint protection, and network traffic.
datasets.caveats: The data is only available in pre-indexed Splunk format for this release. The data may contain profanity or offensive language kept from the scenarios.

datasets.name: Splunk Boss of the SOC v3 (BOTSv3)
datasets.description: BOTSv3 is a Splunk capture-the-flag (CTF) dataset with more than 100 source types. It adds cloud logs from Amazon Web Services (AWS), Azure, and Office 365.
datasets.caveats: It requires Splunk and more than 20 add-ons to parse all source types. Challenge questions are distributed separately from the dataset through the Splunk scoreboard.

datasets.name: StreamSpot
datasets.description: StreamSpot provides provenance graphs from benign browsing and application scenarios and one drive-by download attack. It supports research on streaming graph anomaly detection for host intrusion.
datasets.caveats: Detection performance on this dataset is largely saturated in recent studies. The data dates from 2016 and has only one attack scenario.

datasets.name: Unraveled
datasets.description: Unraveled is a semi-synthetic dataset that follows an advanced persistent threat (APT) campaign from both views. It combines host logs and network flows from a cloud-based emulated organization.
datasets.caveats: User behavior is scripted, so benign activity may be more regular than real traffic.

datasets.name: USENIX CFDR HPC4 Logs (BGL and Thunderbird)
datasets.description: The Computer Failure Data Repository (CFDR) hosts supercomputer logs from Blue Gene/L (BGL), Thunderbird, and three other systems. Messages carry alert category tags that researchers use as anomaly labels.
datasets.dataType: Raw system logs with alert tags
datasets.size: BGL 60 MB and Thunderbird 1.9 GB compressed
datasets.caveats: Alerts describe hardware and software faults and do not represent attacks. The logs are nearly 20 years old and come from retired systems.

datasets.name: 4SICS ICS Lab PCAPs
datasets.description: Netresec captured network traffic in the ICS lab at the 4SICS conference in Stockholm. The captures include Modbus, DNP3, and other industrial protocols from real control devices.
datasets.caveats: The captures are unlabeled and come from a conference lab. They suit protocol analysis and teaching more than benchmark evaluation.

datasets.name: BATADAL
datasets.description: The Battle of the Attack Detection Algorithms (BATADAL) data simulates SCADA readings from the C-Town water distribution network. It provides attack-free training data, partially labeled attack data, and a test set.
datasets.caveats: All data is simulated with hydraulic modeling rather than measured from a real utility. Some attacks in the second training set are only approximately labeled.

datasets.name: BoT-IoT
datasets.description: BoT-IoT contains normal and botnet traffic from a simulated IoT network in the UNSW Canberra Cyber Range. The attacks include DDoS, DoS, scanning, keylogging, and data exfiltration.
datasets.license: Free for academic research, commercial use requires author agreement
datasets.caveats: Attack records vastly outnumber normal records, which inverts typical class imbalance. Most IoT devices in the testbed were simulated rather than physical hardware.

datasets.name: Car-Hacking Dataset (HCRL)
datasets.description: The Hacking and Countermeasure Research Lab (HCRL) logged CAN traffic through the OBD-II port of a real vehicle. The data includes DoS, fuzzy, gear spoofing, and RPM spoofing injection attacks.
datasets.caveats: Data comes from a single vehicle, and injected messages arrive at fixed high rates such as every millisecond. The lab notes errors in Table 2 of the original PST paper.

datasets.name: CIC IoT-DIAD 2024
datasets.description: CIC IoT-DIAD 2024 supports both IoT device identification and anomaly detection from the same captures. It provides flow-based and packet-based features extracted from PCAP files.
datasets.caveats: Traffic comes from a lab testbed and may not match home or industrial deployments. Features come in two extraction formats, so results depend on the chosen format.

datasets.name: CIC Modbus Dataset 2023
datasets.description: The CIC Modbus dataset contains network captures and logs from a simulated electrical substation using the Modbus protocol. Attacks come from external devices, a compromised intelligent electronic device (IED), and a compromised HMI.
datasets.caveats: The substation network is simulated rather than a live utility system. PCAP timestamps use Atlantic Daylight Time and must be aligned with log files.

datasets.name: CICIoMT2024
datasets.description: CICIoMT2024 contains traffic from 18 attacks against a testbed of 40 Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices. It covers Wi-Fi, MQTT, and Bluetooth protocols for healthcare device security research.
datasets.caveats: Fifteen of the 40 devices are simulated rather than physical medical hardware. Attacks fall into five classes that differ widely in record counts.

datasets.name: CICIoT2023
datasets.description: CICIoT2023 contains traffic from 33 attacks executed in an Internet of Things (IoT) topology of 105 devices. The seven attack classes are DDoS, DoS, reconnaissance, web-based, brute force, spoofing, and Mirai.
datasets.caveats: DDoS and DoS records dominate the class distribution of the released data. Attacks were run in a lab, so benign traffic is limited in volume and variety.

datasets.name: CICIoV2024
datasets.description: CICIoV2024 contains Controller Area Network (CAN) bus traffic captured from the electronic control units of a 2019 Ford vehicle. It includes benign messages plus DoS and spoofing attacks for Internet of Vehicles (IoV) research.
datasets.caveats: Data comes from one vehicle model, which limits generalization to other vehicles. The CAN message structure is simple, so detection scores may be optimistic.

datasets.name: Edge-IIoTset
datasets.description: Edge-IIoTset contains traffic from an IoT and IIoT testbed with more than ten device types and fourteen attacks. It supports centralized and federated learning approaches to intrusion detection.
datasets.caveats: Attacks were generated in a lab and may not reflect production IIoT systems. The IEEE DataPort copy requires a paid subscription, so the authors' Kaggle copy is listed.

datasets.name: HAI (HIL-based Augmented ICS) Security Dataset
datasets.description: HAI contains time-series process data from a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testbed combining turbine, boiler, and water treatment processes. Releases from 2020 to 2023 include normal operation and labeled attacks.
datasets.caveats: Versions differ in attacks, tags, and label columns, so results are not comparable across versions. Files from version 22.04 onward require Git LFS to download.

datasets.name: IoT-23
datasets.description: IoT-23 contains 20 malware captures from infected IoT devices and 3 captures of benign IoT devices. Each capture includes the PCAP and a Zeek connection log with malicious and benign labels.
datasets.size: 20 GB full, 8.8 GB labeled flows only
datasets.caveats: A few scenarios contribute most of the flows, and port scan labels dominate. Only 3 of the 23 captures contain benign traffic from uninfected devices.

datasets.name: Kitsune Network Attack Dataset
datasets.description: The Kitsune dataset contains nine network captures of attacks on an IoT and video surveillance network. Each capture has per-packet features, labels, and the original packet capture.
datasets.caveats: Packets in the raw captures were truncated to 200 bytes for privacy. Each capture contains a single attack type, which simplifies the detection task.

datasets.name: Mississippi State ICS Attack Datasets (Gas Pipeline and Power System)
datasets.description: Tommy Morris and colleagues released SCADA (supervisory control and data acquisition) datasets from gas pipeline, water tank, and power testbeds. The data supports intrusion detection research for industrial control systems (ICS).
datasets.caveats: The authors warn that some datasets contain unintended patterns that make attacks trivially separable. The testbeds are small laboratory systems rather than operational plants.

datasets.name: MQTT-IoT-IDS2020
datasets.description: MQTT-IoT-IDS2020 contains traffic from a simulated network using MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport). It includes aggressive scan, UDP scan, SSH brute force, and MQTT brute force scenarios for IoT IDS research.
datasets.caveats: Sensors were simulated, and the attack set covers only four scenarios. Downloading the files requires a free account on the IEEE DataPort site.

datasets.name: MQTTset
datasets.description: MQTTset contains traffic from IoT sensors communicating through an MQTT broker, plus several MQTT-specific attacks. It supports machine learning detection of attacks on MQTT networks.
datasets.caveats: The sensor network was simulated with a fixed set of sensor types. Kaggle requires a free user account before files can be downloaded.

datasets.name: N-BaIoT
datasets.description: N-BaIoT contains traffic features from nine commercial IoT devices infected by Mirai and BASHLITE botnets. Researchers use it for per-device anomaly detection of IoT botnet attacks.
datasets.caveats: Only precomputed statistical features are released, so raw packets are unavailable. Published models often reach near-perfect accuracy, so the benchmark offers limited challenge.

datasets.name: SWaT (Secure Water Treatment)
datasets.description: SWaT contains sensor, actuator, and network data from a six-stage water treatment testbed at SUTD iTrust. The main release covers 51 sensors and actuators over 11 days, with 41 attacks on 4 days.
datasets.license: Free for research with credit to iTrust
datasets.caveats: Version 0 of the normal data starts during a 30-minute tank emptying transient. Since July 2022, the iTrust team no longer answers questions about its datasets.

datasets.name: TON_IoT
datasets.description: TON_IoT combines IoT and IIoT (Industrial IoT) sensor telemetry, Windows and Linux host data, and network traffic from one testbed. Researchers use it for intrusion detection, threat hunting, and digital forensics.
datasets.license: Free for academic research, commercial use requires author permission
datasets.caveats: Labels were assigned by tagging attacker IP addresses and timestamps. Booij et al. (2021) discuss heterogeneity of its features and attack types across the subsets.

datasets.name: UNSW IoT Traffic Traces
datasets.description: The UNSW IoT Analytics group released 20 daily traces from a smart environment testbed with consumer IoT devices. The data supports device identification and profiling from network traffic.
datasets.caveats: The traces contain no attack labels and suit device profiling rather than intrusion detection. Device firmware and cloud endpoints have changed since the 2016 capture period.

datasets.name: WADI (Water Distribution)
datasets.description: WADI contains 16 days of data from the iTrust water distribution testbed with 123 sensors and actuators. The release covers 14 normal days and 2 days with 15 attacks.
datasets.license: Free for research with credit to iTrust
datasets.caveats: The plant was unstable during some periods, and iTrust removed affected readings in a revised file. Attack labels were added in a separate file after the first release.

datasets.name: WUSTL-EHMS-2020
datasets.description: WUSTL-EHMS-2020 combines network flow metrics and patient biometric readings from an enhanced healthcare monitoring system testbed. It supports intrusion detection using both network and medical data.
datasets.caveats: The dataset is small and comes from a single healthcare monitoring testbed. Labels were assigned by attacker MAC address, so address fields should be removed before training.

datasets.name: WUSTL-IIoT-2021
datasets.description: WUSTL-IIoT-2021 contains network flow data from an IIoT testbed that emulates industrial production systems. The attacks include command injection, reconnaissance, and DoS against the testbed.
datasets.caveats: About 92.7 percent of records are normal traffic, so classes are highly imbalanced. The authors advise dropping address and time columns that reveal attack labels.

datasets.name: AndroZoo
datasets.description: AndroZoo is a large collection of Android Package (APK) files gathered from Google Play and other markets. Each app includes antivirus scan results that support malware and benign labeling.
datasets.caveats: API keys require a request from an institutional email and expire after six months. Downloads are capped at 500,000 APKs during each six-month key period. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: Assemblage
datasets.description: Assemblage is a corpus of compiled binaries built from open-source C, C++, and Rust projects. Many binaries include debug information that links code back to source.
datasets.dataType: Windows PE and Linux ELF binaries with debug data
datasets.license: MIT for tools, each binary keeps its source license
datasets.caveats: The corpus is benign only and needs pairing with malware for detection tasks. Build settings may differ from those used for real commercial software.

datasets.name: Avast-CTU Public CAPEv2 Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset from Avast and Czech Technical University (CTU) holds CAPEv2 sandbox reports for malicious Windows files. Reports cover ten malware families and six malware types, including banking Trojans and keyloggers.
datasets.dataType: CAPEv2 JSON reports, full and reduced
datasets.size: 48,976 reports, 13 GB full or 566 MB reduced
datasets.caveats: Malware binaries are not included, so only reports are available. Two families, Emotet and Swisyn, make up over half of all samples.

datasets.name: BinKit
datasets.description: BinKit is a benchmark for binary code similarity analysis built from GNU packages. It compiles each package across compilers, optimization levels, and architectures.
datasets.dataType: Compiled ELF binaries and extracted features
datasets.caveats: The binaries are all benign and target the Linux operating system only. Source packages are limited to GNU projects, which narrows code diversity.

datasets.name: BODMAS
datasets.subcategory: Windows PE malware with family labels
datasets.description: BODMAS is a timestamped Windows Portable Executable (PE) dataset built for temporal analysis of malware classifiers. It provides EMBER-compatible features and family labels for malicious samples.
datasets.dataType: Feature vectors, metadata, malware binaries on request
datasets.size: 57,293 malware and 77,142 benign samples across 581 families
datasets.license: Research use with citation, no redistribution
datasets.caveats: Features and metadata are public, but malware binaries require an email request with affiliation checks. Benign binaries are not shared with requesters because of software copyright concerns. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: CCCS-CIC-AndMal-2020
datasets.subcategory: Android malware static and dynamic features
datasets.description: This dataset from the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS) and CIC covers 14 Android malware categories. It provides static manifest features and dynamic features from memory, application programming interface (API) calls, network, and logs.
datasets.size: 400,000 apps, half benign and half malware, 191 families
datasets.caveats: Labels come from VirusTotal detections and may contain some labeling noise. Some malware families have very few samples, which limits family-level classification.

datasets.name: CIC-AndMal2017
datasets.description: CIC-AndMal2017 captures network traffic from Android malware and benign apps run on real devices. It covers adware, ransomware, scareware, and Short Message Service (SMS) malware across 42 families.
datasets.dataType: PCAP files and flow features, APKs
datasets.caveats: Flow features alone give weak family separation in later studies. The companion CIC-InvesAndMal2019 release adds API call sequences and device logs. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: CIC-Evasive-PDFMal2022
datasets.description: CIC-Evasive-PDFMal2022 targets detection of evasive malicious Portable Document Format (PDF) files. It provides general and structural features for benign and malicious documents.
datasets.caveats: The dataset contains 37 static features only and no raw PDF files. Evasive samples were chosen to reduce overlap with older PDF datasets.

datasets.name: CIC-MalMem-2022
datasets.description: CIC-MalMem-2022 targets detection of obfuscated Windows malware through analysis of memory dumps. It balances benign records with spyware, ransomware, and Trojan families.
datasets.size: 58,596 records, half benign and half malicious
datasets.caveats: The release uses features extracted from memory dumps rather than full dumps. Each malicious category contains only five families, which limits family diversity.

datasets.name: CICMalDroid 2020
datasets.description: CICMalDroid 2020 from the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC) covers four Android malware categories and benign apps. It includes Android Package (APK) files, dynamic analysis logs, and static and dynamic feature files.
datasets.dataType: APKs, dynamic logs (JSON), feature CSVs, PCAP files
datasets.size: About 17,341 APKs, 11,598 in the feature sets
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Not every APK completed dynamic analysis, so feature files cover a subset.

datasets.name: DikeDataset
datasets.description: DikeDataset contains benign and malicious Portable Executable (PE) and Object Linking and Embedding (OLE) files. Each file has a malice score and family membership scores.
datasets.dataType: PE and OLE binaries with labels
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Antivirus software may flag, quarantine, or delete files during download.

datasets.name: Drebin
datasets.description: Drebin is a classic Android malware dataset collected for explainable malware detection research. It groups the malicious Android samples into named malware families for classification.
datasets.dataType: Android APK malware samples and features
datasets.caveats: The samples are more than ten years old and target outdated Android versions. Access requires an email request with identity and advisor verification. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: EMBER 2017 and 2018
datasets.description: The Endgame Malware BEnchmark for Research (EMBER) provides static features from Windows Portable Executable (PE) files. Each release pairs extracted features with benign, malicious, or unlabeled tags for supervised learning.
datasets.size: About 1.1 million PE files (2017) and 1 million PE files (2018)
datasets.timeSpan: Samples first seen in or before 2017 and 2018
datasets.license: MIT for data files, AGPL-3.0 for code
datasets.caveats: The public release contains extracted features only and includes no raw binary files. The two releases used different sample selection criteria and feature versions. The repository was archived in 2026 and is now read-only.

datasets.name: EMBER2024
datasets.description: EMBER2024 is a benchmark of features and labels for files seen on VirusTotal between 2023 and 2024. It covers six file formats and supports detection, family, behavior, packer, and threat group tasks.
datasets.dataType: Extracted features, labels, and baseline models
datasets.size: About 3.2 million files across Win32, Win64, .NET, APK, ELF, and PDF
datasets.caveats: The release contains features and labels but no raw binaries. Labels derive from antivirus detections and may carry some noise.

datasets.name: IoTPOT Malware Dataset
datasets.description: IoTPOT is a honeypot from Yokohama National University that captures Internet of Things (IoT) malware. Shared data include captured Linux Executable and Linkable Format (ELF) binaries and the malware download URLs observed.
datasets.dataType: ELF malware binaries and download URLs
datasets.size: About 16,000 files for 2024 plus X-Pot captures
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Access requires a data request form that the operators review before sharing. Samples are dominated by Mirai and Gafgyt variants that target weak IoT credentials.

datasets.name: KronoDroid
datasets.description: KronoDroid is a hybrid Android dataset with static and dynamic features and timestamps for each app. It includes separate captures from an emulator and from real devices.
datasets.dataType: Feature CSVs, raw logs and APKs on request
datasets.size: About 78,000 real-device and 64,000 emulator samples, 240 families
datasets.caveats: Feature CSVs are public, but raw logs and Android Package (APK) files require researcher verification. The repository has no formal license file beyond the citation request. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: Mal-API-2019
datasets.description: Mal-API-2019 contains Windows application programming interface (API) call sequences recorded from malware in the Cuckoo sandbox. Each sequence carries one of eight malware type labels such as Trojan or worm.
datasets.caveats: The dataset has no benign samples, so it cannot support detection tasks alone. Class labels come from antivirus names and are coarse malware type categories.

datasets.name: MalDICT
datasets.subcategory: Malware behaviors, platforms, exploits, and packers
datasets.description: MalDICT provides four tagged malware benchmarks covering behaviors, target platforms, exploited vulnerabilities, and packers. Tags come from antivirus results and use a temporal train and test split.
datasets.dataType: File hashes, tags, EMBER features, disarmed PE binaries
datasets.size: About 4.3 million files in the behavior set plus smaller platform, vulnerability, and packer sets
datasets.caveats: Only Portable Executable (PE) binaries are published, and other files must be fetched from VirusShare by hash. Tags derive from antivirus labels and therefore carry some amount of label noise. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: MaleVis
datasets.description: MaleVis provides RGB byte images of Windows malware and legitimate software for vision research. Images come in two resolutions for convolutional neural network (CNN) experiments.
datasets.caveats: Access requires a short Google Form registration before the download link appears. Only images are shared, and binaries require direct contact with the authors.

datasets.name: MaleX
datasets.description: MaleX is a curated set of Windows executables with malware and benign labels. It releases frequency-domain images and extracted features for image-based malware detection.
datasets.caveats: The underlying executable binaries are not currently available for download. Access requires a form that asks for affiliation and intended research use.

datasets.name: Malimg
datasets.description: Malimg converts Windows malware binaries into grayscale byteplot images for visual classification. It is a common baseline dataset for image-based malware classification research.
datasets.caveats: The download link comes from the authors' company page in the MaleX repository. Many studies report near-perfect accuracy, so the benchmark is largely saturated. The underlying samples date from 2011 and do not reflect current malware.

datasets.name: MalNet
datasets.description: MalNet provides function call graphs and binary images derived from Android Package (APK) files in AndroZoo. It supports graph learning and image-based malware type and family classification.
datasets.dataType: Function call graphs and byteplot images
datasets.size: About 1.2 million graphs and 1.2 million images across 47 types and 696 families
datasets.caveats: Labels come from antivirus detections and therefore carry some labeling noise. Class distribution is highly imbalanced across the malware types and families.

datasets.name: MalShare
datasets.description: MalShare is a community malware repository that has operated since 2013. Registered users can search, upload, and download samples through the site or its API.
datasets.dataType: Malware samples and daily hash lists
datasets.license: Terms of service on the site
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Samples are user submissions and carry only limited labels or family information.

datasets.name: MalwareBazaar
datasets.description: MalwareBazaar is an abuse.ch project that collects and shares malware samples with tags and signatures. Users can query samples and download them through the web interface or an application programming interface (API).
datasets.dataType: Malware samples, hashes, tags, and vendor intelligence
datasets.license: Terms of service on the site
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Programmatic API use requires a free authentication key from the abuse.ch portal. Samples reflect community submissions rather than a balanced research sample.

datasets.name: MH-100K
datasets.description: MH-100K is an Android dataset with permissions, application programming interface (API) calls, intents, and VirusTotal results for each app. All apps were drawn from the AndroZoo repository and scanned with VirusTotal.
datasets.caveats: Malware labels depend on a threshold of four VirusTotal detections. The class balance is heavily skewed toward benign apps over malicious ones.

datasets.name: Microsoft Malware Classification Challenge (BIG 2015)
datasets.description: This Kaggle challenge released Windows malware as hexadecimal byte dumps and disassembly files. Researchers use it as a standard benchmark for malware family classification.
datasets.dataType: Hex byte dumps and IDA disassembly (.asm) files
datasets.size: About 21,700 samples in 9 families, nearly 0.5 TB uncompressed
datasets.caveats: Headers were removed, so the files cannot run and header analysis is not possible. Labels for the Kaggle test set were never released to the public. The samples date from 2015 and do not reflect current threats.

datasets.name: Microsoft Malware Prediction
datasets.description: This Kaggle competition dataset predicts whether a Windows machine will encounter malware. Each row describes machine properties from Windows Defender heartbeat and threat telemetry.
datasets.size: About 8.9 million training rows with 83 features
datasets.caveats: The data describes machine configurations and does not include any malware files. The training and test sets differ in time, which causes distribution shift.

datasets.name: MOTIF
datasets.description: The Malware Open-source Threat Intelligence Family (MOTIF) dataset links Portable Executable (PE) malware to families named in public threat reports. It offers disarmed binaries and EMBER features with report-based family labels.
datasets.dataType: Disarmed PE binaries, EMBER v2 features, family labels
datasets.size: 3,095 samples from 454 families, about 1.47 GB compressed
datasets.caveats: Samples are disarmed to block execution but still contain real malicious code. Many families have only a few samples, which limits per-family training. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: RanSAP
datasets.description: RanSAP records low-level storage access patterns from ransomware and benign programs on Windows. Data were collected through a hypervisor on hard disk and solid state drive setups.
datasets.dataType: Storage read and write traces with entropy
datasets.size: 7 ransomware samples, 21 extra variants, 5 benign programs
datasets.caveats: The sample count is small and uses mainly Windows 7 hosts. The no-derivatives license limits sharing of modified or derived versions of the data.

datasets.name: RISS Ransomware Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset from the Research Institute in Information Security (RISS) records early dynamic behavior of ransomware and goodware. Features come from Cuckoo sandbox runs that monitor the first phases of execution.
datasets.caveats: The samples date from 2016 and miss modern ransomware families. Only extracted features are shared, and the original binaries are not included.

datasets.name: SOREL-20M
datasets.subcategory: Windows PE malware samples and features
datasets.description: The Sophos-ReversingLabs 20 Million dataset (SOREL-20M) supports research on malicious Portable Executable (PE) file detection. It offers labels, EMBER features, and disarmed binaries on Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3).
datasets.dataType: Disarmed PE binaries, EMBER v2 features, PE metadata
datasets.size: About 20 million samples, roughly 8 TB with binaries
datasets.caveats: Binaries are disarmed by zeroing header fields but still contain real malicious code. Benign binaries are not distributed because of intellectual property limits. The full download is very large and needs substantial storage. Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment.

datasets.name: theZoo
datasets.description: theZoo is a public GitHub repository of live malware binaries and source code for education. Each sample ships in a password-protected archive with matching hash and password files.
datasets.dataType: Encrypted malware binaries and source code
datasets.license: GPL-3.0 for code, which excludes the malware samples
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Some samples are worms that can spread automatically across connected networks. Coverage is curated and uneven, so it suits teaching more than training models.

datasets.name: VirusShare
datasets.description: VirusShare is a long-running repository of malware samples for researchers and incident responders. Hash lists and sample archives support large-scale malware corpus construction.
datasets.caveats: Contains live malware. Handle only in an isolated lab environment. Accounts are granted by invitation after a request to the operator. Samples come without family labels and without any benign counterparts for comparison.

datasets.name: 5G-NIDD
datasets.description: 5G-NIDD contains traffic from a 5G test network at the University of Oulu with two base stations. Attacker nodes launch DoS floods and port scans against a server in the mobile edge environment.
datasets.size: About 3.6 GB PCAP across two base stations
datasets.caveats: The attack set is limited to DoS floods and port scans. Downloading the files requires a free account on the IEEE DataPort site.

datasets.name: AWID3
datasets.description: AWID3 contains IEEE 802.11 enterprise wireless traffic with attacks such as deauthentication, evil twin, and website spoofing. It also includes common wired-network attacks and a CSV version with 254 features.
datasets.caveats: Data comes from a small lab testbed with a limited set of devices. Access requires submitting a download request form to the dataset authors.

datasets.name: CAIDA Anonymized Internet Traces
datasets.description: CAIDA collected anonymized packet header traces from high-speed commercial backbone links in the United States. Researchers use them to study internet traffic characteristics and build realistic baselines.
datasets.caveats: Packet payloads are removed and IP addresses are anonymized before release. Collection ended in January 2019, so the traces do not reflect current traffic.

datasets.name: CAIDA DDoS Attack 2007
datasets.description: The Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA) released one hour of anonymized traffic from a real DDoS attack. The trace holds only attack traffic to the victim and its responses.
datasets.caveats: The trace is old and covers a single attack event. Non-attack traffic was removed, so it cannot train a benign baseline alone.

datasets.name: CESNET-QUIC22
datasets.description: CESNET-QUIC22 contains one month of QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections) flows from Czech national backbone links. Labels identify web services, which supports classification of encrypted QUIC traffic.
datasets.caveats: Service labels are derived from server names seen in handshakes and may contain errors. The dataset has no attack labels and suits traffic classification rather than intrusion detection.

datasets.name: CESNET-TLS-Year22
datasets.description: CESNET-TLS-Year22 contains a full year of TLS (Transport Layer Security) flows from Czech backbone lines. It supports encrypted traffic classification and studies of model drift over time.
datasets.caveats: Labels identify services rather than malicious behavior, so the data does not support attack detection directly. The CESNET DataZoo Python library is recommended for handling the data volume.

datasets.name: CIC-Bell-DNS 2021
datasets.description: CIC-Bell-DNS 2021 contains DNS features for 400,000 benign and 13,011 malicious domain samples. Labels separate spam, phishing, and malware domains for malicious domain classification research.
datasets.caveats: Domain labels come from public blocklists that may contain stale or wrong entries. Benign samples far outnumber malicious samples, which creates strong class imbalance.

datasets.name: CIC-Bell-DNS-EXF-2021
datasets.description: CIC-Bell-DNS-EXF-2021 contains DNS traffic generated by exfiltrating files of varied sizes through DNS queries. It provides 30 stateless and stateful features for detecting DNS data exfiltration.
datasets.caveats: Exfiltration traffic was produced with the DNSExfiltrator tool using fixed encoding and throttling settings. Real attackers may use different encodings, tools, and timing patterns.

datasets.name: CIC-Darknet2020
datasets.description: CIC-Darknet2020 combines ISCXTor2016 and ISCXVPN2016 into one darknet traffic dataset with two label layers. It supports detecting Tor and VPN traffic and classifying the underlying application type.
datasets.caveats: The dataset reuses 2016 captures and inherits their lab generation limits. Here darknet means Tor and VPN traffic, not network telescope data.

datasets.name: CIC-DDoS2019
datasets.description: CIC-DDoS2019 contains benign traffic and 12 reflection and exploitation DDoS attacks over two capture days. Attacks include NTP, DNS, LDAP, MSSQL, NetBIOS, SNMP, SSDP, UDP, and SYN floods.
datasets.caveats: Flows were generated with CICFlowMeter-V3, the tool linked to documented labeling errors in CIC-IDS2017. Attack flows vastly outnumber benign flows in the released CSV files.

datasets.name: CIC-IDS2017
datasets.description: CIC-IDS2017 holds five days of emulated enterprise traffic with benign activity and common network attacks. It provides packet capture (PCAP) files and labeled flow features for training intrusion detection systems (IDS).
datasets.license: Public for researchers with citation required
datasets.caveats: Engelen et al. (2021) documented flow construction and labeling errors in the released CSV files. Benign traffic comes from scripted user profiles rather than real users. Attack classes such as Heartbleed and infiltration have very few samples.

datasets.name: CIDDS-001 and CIDDS-002
datasets.description: The Coburg Intrusion Detection Data Sets (CIDDS) contain labeled NetFlow data from an emulated small business network in OpenStack. Scripts generate benign user behavior, and the attacks include DoS, brute force, and port scans.
datasets.caveats: Benign traffic is emulated by Python scripts rather than real users. Public IP addresses are anonymized, and only flow data is released.

datasets.name: CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020
datasets.description: CIRA-CIC-DoHBrw-2020 captures benign DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) traffic, malicious DoH tunnels, and non-DoH HTTPS browsing. It supports two-layer classification of encrypted DNS traffic with statistical and time-series features.
datasets.caveats: Malicious DoH traffic comes from three tunneling tools in a lab setting. Models may learn tool signatures rather than general tunnel behavior.

datasets.name: CSE-CIC-IDS2018
datasets.description: CSE-CIC-IDS2018 contains traffic and host logs from a simulated organization with 420 machines and 30 servers. It covers seven attack scenarios, including brute force, botnet, DoS (denial of service), and web attacks, for IDS benchmarking.
datasets.license: Redistribution allowed with citation and link to the AWS page
datasets.caveats: Liu et al. (2022) reported labeling and flow extraction errors similar to those found in CIC-IDS2017. Download requires the AWS command line tool and substantial storage.

datasets.name: CTU-13
datasets.description: CTU-13 contains 13 scenarios of real botnet traffic mixed with normal and background traffic at CTU University. Each scenario provides labeled bidirectional NetFlows and botnet-only packet captures.
datasets.caveats: The botnet families and network conditions date from 2011 and are now dated. Full PCAPs with background traffic are withheld for privacy reasons. Background flows carry no verified benign or malicious label in any scenario.

datasets.name: CyberLab Honeynet Dataset
datasets.description: The CyberLab dataset contains logs from Cowrie SSH and Telnet honeypots on about 50 nodes. The logs record attacker sessions, commands, and downloaded files for threat research.
datasets.caveats: Public IP addresses are pseudonymized to protect the honeypot nodes. The number of active nodes changed during the experiment, which affects volume comparisons over time.

datasets.name: DARPA 1998 and 1999 Intrusion Detection Evaluation
datasets.description: MIT Lincoln Laboratory released the DARPA (Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency) evaluation data with simulated network traffic and audit logs. It contains weeks of labeled attacks and attack-free weeks for training anomaly detectors.
datasets.caveats: This dataset is outdated and reflects network services and attacks from the late 1990s. McHugh (2000) criticized its synthetic background traffic and simulation artifacts. The 1999 data sits on a companion Lincoln Laboratory page.

datasets.name: DARPA Operationally Transparent Cyber (OpTC)
datasets.description: OpTC contains endpoint telemetry and Zeek network logs from a DARPA pilot that scaled monitoring to about one thousand hosts. It includes a red team scenario for studying attack detection across hosts.
datasets.caveats: The data is hosted on Google Drive and is very large. DARPA released it as is, without support or accuracy warranties.

datasets.name: HIKARI-2021
datasets.description: HIKARI-2021 combines real benign traffic with synthetic attacks carried over encrypted HTTPS sessions. It targets intrusion detection when payloads are encrypted and only flow features are usable.
datasets.caveats: Attack traffic is synthetic and generated in a lab setting. Attack classes are limited to brute force, probing, and cryptomining traffic.

datasets.name: ISCX Botnet 2014
datasets.description: ISCX Botnet 2014 merges traces from ISOT, ISCX-IDS2012, and the Malware Capture Facility Project into training and test sets. It supports evaluating botnet detection with 7 training and 16 test botnet types.
datasets.caveats: The dataset was built with an overlay method that maps botnet IP addresses into merged traces. Merging traces from different sources can leave artifacts that make detection easier.

datasets.name: ISCX Tor-nonTor 2016
datasets.description: ISCXTor2016 contains Tor and regular traffic for browsing, email, chat, streaming, file transfer, VoIP, and P2P activities. It supports detecting Tor use and classifying applications inside Tor traffic.
datasets.license: Public for researchers with citation required
datasets.caveats: The traffic reflects Tor and application versions that were current in 2016. Lab generation by a few users limits the diversity of behavior in the data.

datasets.name: ISCX VPN-nonVPN 2016
datasets.description: ISCXVPN2016 captures regular and VPN (virtual private network) sessions across 14 traffic categories such as VoIP and streaming. It supports classification of encrypted and VPN traffic using time-related flow features.
datasets.license: Public for researchers with citation required
datasets.caveats: Traffic was generated by a small set of lab users and applications in 2016. Application versions and VPN protocols have changed considerably since the capture period.

datasets.name: ISCX-IDS2012
datasets.description: ISCX-IDS2012 records seven days of testbed network activity at the University of New Brunswick. Attacks include infiltration, HTTP denial of service, IRC botnet DDoS (distributed denial of service), and SSH brute force.
datasets.size: About 84 GB PCAP across seven days
datasets.caveats: The traffic dates from 2010 and lacks modern protocols and attack types. Each day contains a single attack scenario, which simplifies detection.

datasets.name: Kyoto 2006+
datasets.description: Kyoto 2006+ contains session records from honeypots and servers deployed at Kyoto University. It provides traffic features and IDS alert labels for network intrusion detection research.
datasets.caveats: The download site refused connections on 2026-10-25; confirm it is back before planning a project around it. Labels depend on IDS and antivirus alerts, which miss unknown attacks. Traffic that reaches honeypots is mostly malicious by design, which differs from enterprise networks.

datasets.name: LANL Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events (2015)
datasets.description: Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL) released 58 consecutive days of de-identified enterprise events. The data includes authentication, process, DNS, and network flow events plus labeled red team compromises.
datasets.caveats: Red team events are very rare compared with normal activity. De-identification removes context such as real usernames and host roles.

datasets.name: LANL Unified Host and Network Dataset (2017)
datasets.description: The LANL Unified Host and Network Dataset combines Windows host event logs and router flow records from one enterprise network. Host and network identities match, which supports joint host and network analysis.
datasets.caveats: The release contains no labeled attacks, so it suits anomaly detection and baseline modeling. Values are de-identified to protect the security of the LANL environment.

datasets.name: LITNET-2020
datasets.description: LITNET-2020 is an annotated flow dataset collected from real traffic on the Lithuanian academic network. It includes normal flows and labeled attack flows for evaluating network intrusion detection methods.
datasets.caveats: Labels on the real traffic depend on the annotation rules the authors applied. Attack classes are much smaller than the volume of normal traffic.

datasets.name: MAWI Working Group Traffic Archive
datasets.description: The MAWI (Measurement and Analysis on the WIDE Internet) archive provides daily traces from the WIDE upstream transit link. It also holds multi-day traces from yearly measurement events for internet traffic research.
datasets.caveats: Traces are anonymized and packet payloads are removed before release. The traces carry no attack labels, so MAWILab labels are often used alongside them.

datasets.name: MAWILab
datasets.description: MAWILab labels traffic anomalies in the MAWI archive by combining the outputs of several anomaly detectors. Researchers use it to benchmark anomaly detectors on real backbone traffic.
datasets.caveats: Labels come from agreement among detectors rather than verified ground truth. Anomalies that every detector misses remain unlabeled in the archive.

datasets.name: NSL-KDD
datasets.description: NSL-KDD is a filtered version of the KDD Cup 1999 data that removes duplicate records. It provides connection-level features and attack labels and remains common in teaching and legacy benchmarks.
datasets.caveats: This dataset is outdated because its traffic comes from the 1998 DARPA evaluation. Results on NSL-KDD rarely transfer to modern network traffic or current attack types.

datasets.name: OpenINTEL
datasets.description: OpenINTEL performs daily active DNS measurements across large parts of the global domain name space. Researchers use it to study DNS infrastructure, abuse, and changes over time.
datasets.caveats: Some zones and closed datasets require a separate request or data sharing agreement. Data volume is very large and needs big data tools.

datasets.name: SANS Internet Storm Center DShield
datasets.description: DShield aggregates firewall logs and honeypot reports submitted by volunteers worldwide. Its public API returns attack sources, targeted ports, and web honeypot data for threat analysis.
datasets.caveats: Sensor coverage depends on volunteers, so geographic and network coverage is uneven. The API asks users to include contact information in requests.

datasets.name: Stratosphere Malware Capture Facility Project (MCFP)
datasets.description: The Malware Capture Facility Project publishes long-term captures of real malware and normal traffic from CTU University. Each capture folder includes packet captures, flow files, and malware details for detection research.
datasets.caveats: Captures vary widely in length, labeling depth, and documentation quality across the archive. The directory listing gives little guidance, so users must read each capture README.

datasets.name: UCSD Network Telescope (CAIDA)
datasets.description: The UCSD Network Telescope captures unsolicited traffic sent to a large block of unused IPv4 addresses. The traces show scanning, backscatter from spoofed DDoS attacks, and malware spread.
datasets.size: More than 3 TB uncompressed per day
datasets.license: CAIDA Acceptable Use Agreement and Telescope Supplement
datasets.caveats: Access requires a request form and an approved research purpose. The daily data volume demands major storage and processing capacity from users.

datasets.name: UGR'16
datasets.description: UGR'16 contains NetFlow v9 records from collectors inside a Spanish internet service provider (ISP). A four-month calibration set holds real background traffic, and a later test set adds synthetic attacks.
datasets.caveats: Later studies report labeling inaccuracies that make measured model performance uncertain. The real background traffic may also contain attacks that carry no label.

datasets.name: UNSW-NB15
datasets.description: UNSW-NB15 contains 100 GB of raw traffic from the UNSW Canberra Cyber Range with nine attack families. It offers PCAP, Argus, Bro logs, and labeled CSV records for training and testing IDS models.
datasets.license: Free for academic research, commercial use requires author agreement
datasets.caveats: Attack traffic was generated synthetically with the IXIA PerfectStorm tool. Several attack families have very few records, which creates strong class imbalance.

datasets.name: UQ NetFlow NIDS datasets (NF-UQ-NIDS)
datasets.description: The University of Queensland converted UNSW-NB15, BoT-IoT, ToN-IoT, and CSE-CIC-IDS2018 into a common NetFlow feature set. Versions 1 to 3 support cross-dataset evaluation of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS).
datasets.caveats: These are derived datasets, so they inherit synthetic traffic and labeling errors from the source datasets. The feature sets differ across versions 1, 2, and 3, so results are not directly comparable.

datasets.name: Enron Email Dataset
datasets.description: Carnegie Mellon University (CMU) hosts this corpus of about 500,000 emails from about 150 Enron employees. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission released the data during its investigation.
datasets.dataType: Raw email messages in folder structure
datasets.caveats: The corpus has no phishing labels, so it usually serves as legitimate email. It contains real personal information, so handle it with care.

datasets.name: ISCX-URL2016
datasets.description: The Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity (CIC) built this dataset of benign and malicious Uniform Resource Locators (URLs). It covers benign, spam, phishing, malware, and defacement URL classes.
datasets.license: Citation required per CIC dataset terms
