datasets.caveats: Downloads pass through a short Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity registration form. The URL sources are older and many links are no longer active.

datasets.name: Nazario Phishing Corpus
datasets.description: Jose Nazario maintains this corpus of hand classified phishing emails from his personal inbox. Files are grouped into mailbox archives by year, with recent files released annually.
datasets.size: Mailbox files from about 3 MB to 31 MB
datasets.caveats: The corpus is representative rather than exhaustive because it comes from one inbox. Later mailboxes are not anonymized and may contain personal data.

datasets.name: OpenPhish Community Feed
datasets.description: OpenPhish publishes a free community feed of phishing Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) found by automated analysis. The community tier updates every 12 hours as a plain text list.
datasets.dataType: Plain text list of phishing URLs
datasets.caveats: The free tier omits brand, network, and historical metadata found in paid tiers. The feed contains live malicious links that can infect systems or steal credentials. Open these links only inside an isolated sandbox or virtual machine and never on production systems.

datasets.name: Phishing Email Curated Datasets
datasets.description: This Zenodo record bundles 11 cleaned email corpora for phishing detection in consistent CSV files. It includes Enron, Ling, CEAS 2008, Nazario, Nigerian fraud, SpamAssassin, and TREC 2005 to 2007.
datasets.dataType: Email text with sender, subject, body, and labels (CSV)
datasets.caveats: The original TREC spam corpus download links now return errors. This Zenodo record offers a practical secondary copy of those corpora for research.

datasets.name: Phishing Websites Dataset (Vrbancic)
datasets.description: This Mendeley Data set provides 88,647 website instances labeled as legitimate or phishing. Each instance carries 111 features derived from the Uniform Resource Locator (URL) and domain.
datasets.caveats: The full and small variants have different class balance between legitimate and phishing. Report which variant you use so others can reproduce your results.

datasets.name: Phishpedia Phishing Benchmark
datasets.description: The Phishpedia project released a benchmark of about 30,000 phishing webpages for visual brand identification research. Each sample includes the URL, HTML, screenshot, and target brand.
datasets.dataType: URLs, HTML, screenshots, and brand labels
datasets.caveats: The data is hosted on Google Drive through a link in the repository. Screenshots show real brand logos, so avoid redistributing them outside research use.

datasets.name: PhishTank
datasets.description: PhishTank is a community database of phishing Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) verified by volunteers. Cisco operates the service and publishes the full database as hourly downloadable files.
datasets.dataType: URLs with submission time, verification status, and target brand (CSV, JSON, XML)
datasets.caveats: Unregistered users are limited to a few downloads per day. The feed contains live malicious links that can infect systems or steal credentials. Open these links only inside an isolated sandbox or virtual machine and never on production systems.

datasets.name: PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset
datasets.description: PhiUSIIL contains 235,795 labeled Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) with features from page source and URL text. The collection includes 134,850 legitimate URLs and 100,945 phishing URLs with 54 features each.
datasets.dataType: Tabular features (54 columns) with binary labels
datasets.caveats: Several features are derived from page content and may leak label information. Check each feature definition before modeling to avoid inflated accuracy.

datasets.name: PhreshPhish
datasets.description: PhreshPhish pairs phishing and benign Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) with full webpage HyperText Markup Language (HTML). The release holds 666,315 samples with train and test splits.
datasets.dataType: URL, HTML, collection date, language, and label
datasets.caveats: Stored HTML may contain credential harvesting forms, tracking code, and malicious scripts. Do not render these pages in a browser outside an isolated sandbox.

datasets.name: SMS Spam Collection
datasets.description: This University of California, Irvine (UCI) dataset holds 5,574 Short Message Service (SMS) messages labeled ham or spam. Messages come mainly from sources in the United Kingdom and in Singapore.
datasets.caveats: The class balance is skewed toward ham, with 747 spam messages overall. The messages predate current smishing campaigns that use links and delivery lures.

datasets.name: SpamAssassin Public Corpus
datasets.description: The Apache SpamAssassin project published this corpus of spam, easy ham, and hard ham email. It remains a common baseline for spam filtering and phishing detection studies.
datasets.size: Nine archives of about 1 to 2 MB each
datasets.caveats: The messages are more than twenty years old and reflect early spam tactics. Modern spam and phishing campaigns look quite different from these samples.

datasets.name: UCI Phishing Websites
datasets.description: This University of California, Irvine (UCI) dataset describes 11,055 websites with 30 engineered phishing indicators. Samples were gathered from PhishTank, MillerSmiles, and Google search results by the dataset authors.
datasets.dataType: Tabular integer features with binary labels
datasets.caveats: The data predates modern phishing kits and the wide adoption of HTTPS encryption. Results from this dataset may not transfer to current phishing attacks.

datasets.name: URLhaus
datasets.description: URLhaus from abuse.ch tracks Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) used to distribute malware. It offers database dumps every five minutes plus a free community Application Programming Interface (API).
datasets.dataType: Malicious URLs with tags, status, and payload hashes (CSV, JSON, MISP, RPZ)
datasets.license: abuse.ch fair use terms, commercial heavy use may require a paid subscription
datasets.caveats: All downloads require a free Auth-Key from the abuse.ch authentication portal. The feed contains live malicious links that can infect systems or steal credentials. Open these links only inside an isolated sandbox or virtual machine and never on production systems.

datasets.name: Web Page Phishing Detection (Hannousse and Yahiouche)
datasets.description: This Mendeley Data set holds 11,430 balanced phishing and legitimate Uniform Resource Locators (URLs). Each URL has 87 features drawn from URL syntax, page content, and external services.
datasets.dataType: URLs, Document Object Model trees, and tabular features
datasets.caveats: External service features such as search rank may not be reproducible today. Recompute these features from current sources before reusing the dataset.

datasets.name: AnnoCTR
datasets.description: AnnoCTR contains cyber threat reports annotated with named entities, temporal expressions, and security concepts. Entities and concepts link to Wikipedia and to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques.
datasets.caveats: The repository is an archived research prototype that the authors do not maintain. Share-alike license terms apply to any derived datasets that researchers distribute.

datasets.name: APTNER
datasets.description: APTNER is a named entity recognition dataset built from cyber threat intelligence reports and security blogs. It defines 21 entity types that align with common threat intelligence concepts.
datasets.size: Train, development, and test files of about 2.4 MB
datasets.caveats: The repository has no license and has not been maintained since 2022. Its label definitions differ from DNRTI and CyNER, so merging datasets needs a label mapping.

datasets.name: CASIE
datasets.description: CASIE (CyberAttack Sensing and Information Extraction) provides news articles annotated with cybersecurity events and arguments. Event types include data breach, phishing, ransom, vulnerability discovery, and patch.
datasets.dataType: JSON annotation and source text files
datasets.caveats: The repository has no license file, so reuse terms should be confirmed with the authors. News articles differ in style and detail from technical threat intelligence reports.

datasets.name: CTIBench
datasets.description: CTIBench evaluates LLMs on practical cyber threat intelligence tasks drawn from real analyst work. Tasks cover CTI knowledge, CVE to CWE mapping, CVSS prediction, ATT&CK extraction, and actor attribution.
datasets.size: 4,610 benchmark examples across five task families
datasets.caveats: Some tasks use public CVE and report text that may already appear in model training data. The repository moved from its original GitHub owner, so older links may redirect.

datasets.name: CTID Mappings Explorer
datasets.subcategory: Control and vulnerability to ATT&CK mappings
datasets.description: The Center for Threat-Informed Defense (CTID) maps security controls and capabilities to ATT&CK techniques. The project also absorbed the earlier CTID mappings from CVE records to ATT&CK.
datasets.dataType: JSON, CSV, and Excel mapping files
datasets.caveats: Mappings reflect analyst judgment and cover only selected ATT&CK versions. Vulnerability mappings cover a small subset of CVEs rather than the full CVE List.

datasets.name: CyberMetric
datasets.description: CyberMetric is a set of multiple-choice questions on cybersecurity knowledge for evaluating language models. Questions were generated with retrieval from standards, papers, and books, then validated by experts.
datasets.caveats: Questions were generated with GPT-3.5, so wording may favor models from similar families. The authors report expert validation, but errors may remain in the larger subsets.

datasets.name: CyNER
datasets.description: CyNER is a Python library for cybersecurity named entity recognition (NER) in threat reports. Its repository includes annotated sentences split into train, validation, and test files.
datasets.caveats: The annotated corpus is small and follows its own entity labeling scheme. Results may not transfer to CTI NER datasets that use different label sets.

datasets.name: DNRTI
datasets.description: DNRTI is a named entity recognition dataset built from more than 300 threat intelligence reports. Experts annotated entities in 13 categories such as hacker organizations, tools, and attack actions.
datasets.dataType: Token-labeled text in a RAR archive
datasets.caveats: The repository has no license and offers minimal documentation beyond the archive itself. Users must check the split files and label conventions before comparing results across papers.

datasets.name: MalwareTextDB
datasets.description: MalwareTextDB annotates APT reports with malware entities, relations, and attribute labels from Malware Attribute Enumeration and Characterization (MAEC). The corpus was later extended for the SemEval-2018 Task 8 shared task.
datasets.dataType: Annotated text in a zip archive
datasets.caveats: The corpus is small and its reports date from 2017 or earlier. The SemEval extension covering 85 reports is distributed separately from this archive.

datasets.name: MITRE ATLAS Data
datasets.description: MITRE ATLAS (Adversarial Threat Landscape for Artificial-Intelligence Systems) describes adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems. The data also includes documented case studies of attacks on machine learning systems.
datasets.size: 170 techniques and sub-techniques and 57 case studies (v5.6.0)
datasets.caveats: The field changes quickly, so technique lists shift noticeably between ATLAS versions. Case studies include research demonstrations as well as incidents observed in real deployments.

datasets.name: MITRE ATT&CK STIX Data
datasets.description: MITRE ATT&CK describes adversary tactics, techniques, groups, and software based on real-world observations. This repository provides the Enterprise, Mobile, and Industrial Control Systems (ICS) domains as Structured Threat Information Expression (STIX) 2.1 bundles.
datasets.size: ATT&CK v19.2 for Enterprise, Mobile, and ICS
datasets.caveats: Technique identifiers change between versions through revocation, deprecation, and restructuring. Studies should record the exact ATT&CK version used for every mapping or label.

datasets.name: MITRE CAPEC
datasets.description: CAPEC catalogs common attack patterns that adversaries use against software, hardware, and communication systems. Entries link to related CWE weaknesses and include prerequisites and mitigations.
datasets.caveats: CAPEC receives updates less often than ATT&CK and can lag behind current attacker behavior. Some attack patterns are abstract and hard to map to observed security events.

datasets.name: MITRE CTI Repository
datasets.description: The MITRE cyber threat intelligence (CTI) repository provides ATT&CK content in the STIX 2.0 format. It also includes Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification (CAPEC) data for tools built on python-stix2.
datasets.caveats: This repository uses STIX 2.0 and lacks the collection features of the newer repository. New projects should prefer attack-stix-data when they need STIX 2.1 ATT&CK content.

datasets.name: MITRE CWE
datasets.description: CWE is a hierarchical list of common software and hardware weakness types maintained by MITRE. It supplies the weakness labels used by NVD and most vulnerable code datasets.
datasets.caveats: CWE labels assigned in NVD records are often coarse, generic, or inconsistent across analysts. Researchers should choose one CWE view, such as View-1003, to aggregate labels consistently.

datasets.name: MITRE D3FEND
datasets.description: D3FEND is a knowledge graph of cybersecurity countermeasures and the digital artifacts they act on. It links defensive techniques to ATT&CK offensive techniques through those shared artifacts.
datasets.caveats: Mappings between defensive and offensive techniques are inferred through artifacts rather than observed outcomes. The ontology structure changes across releases, so pin a specific version.

datasets.name: Primus-FineWeb
datasets.description: Primus-FineWeb is a cybersecurity text corpus filtered from the FineWeb web crawl with a trained classifier. It supports continued pretraining of language models for security tasks.
datasets.dataType: Text records in a Hugging Face dataset
datasets.caveats: Access requires a Hugging Face login and agreement to share contact information. Users must also follow the FineWeb license and the Common Crawl terms of use.

datasets.name: Sigma Rules
datasets.description: Sigma is a generic signature format for writing log-based detection rules across security platforms. The main repository holds community detection rules tagged with ATT&CK techniques.
datasets.caveats: Rule quality and false positive rates vary by author and by log source. The Detection Rule License (DRL) requires attribution when rules are reused or converted.

datasets.name: TRAM Training Data
datasets.description: The Threat Report ATT&CK Mapper (TRAM) repository includes annotated CTI reports for training technique classifiers. The shipped model identifies up to 50 common ATT&CK techniques in report text.
datasets.caveats: The training data covers a limited technique subset and targets ATT&CK version 13. Newer ATT&CK releases have renamed or restructured some techniques used in these labels.

datasets.name: abuse.ch Feodo Tracker
datasets.description: Feodo Tracker lists botnet command and control (C2) servers for malware families that grew from banking trojans. Blocklists include IP addresses with first seen and last online dates.
datasets.caveats: Blocklists show currently tracked C2 servers, so historical research needs regular snapshots. The abuse.ch fair use limits and commercial terms apply to all automated access.

datasets.name: abuse.ch SSL Blacklist (SSLBL)
datasets.description: The abuse.ch blocklist SSLBL lists Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certificates used by botnet C2 servers and malware. Entries include certificate SHA1 fingerprints together with the associated malware family names.
datasets.caveats: Coverage reflects what abuse.ch observes and does not include all malicious certificates. The abuse.ch fair use limits and commercial terms apply to all automated access.

datasets.name: abuse.ch ThreatFox
datasets.description: ThreatFox is an abuse.ch platform for sharing indicators of compromise (IOCs) linked to malware. Indicators include IP addresses, domains, URLs, and file hashes with malware family tags.
datasets.dataType: CSV and JSON exports plus REST API
datasets.caveats: Access requires an abuse.ch account and a personal Auth-Key for API queries. Indicators are submitted by the community and can include false positives or stale entries. Commercial use requires a paid subscription that Spamhaus manages on behalf of abuse.ch.

datasets.name: abuse.ch URLhaus
datasets.description: URLhaus is an abuse.ch project that collects URLs used to distribute malware. Entries include online status, tags, payload hashes, and the reporter who submitted each URL.
datasets.dataType: CSV, JSON, and text exports plus REST API
datasets.caveats: Access now requires an authenticated abuse.ch account and a personal Auth-Key for queries. Free use covers non-commercial volumes, and commercial use needs a paid Spamhaus subscription.

datasets.name: APT and Cybercriminal Campaign Collections (CyberMonitor)
datasets.description: CyberMonitor collects public reports on APT and cybercriminal campaigns organized by publication year. The repository stores report files alongside an index in its main README file.
datasets.caveats: The collection was last updated in July 2024 and may not receive further additions. Reports remain under their publishers' copyrights, and some files may trigger antivirus alerts.

datasets.name: APTnotes
datasets.description: APTnotes indexes public vendor reports on campaigns attributed to advanced persistent threat (APT) groups. A CSV file lists the title, source, link, hash, and date for each report.
datasets.dataType: CSV and JSON index with PDF reports
datasets.caveats: Report PDFs are hosted on Box and require the separate download tools in aptnotes/tools. Vendor reports carry their own copyrights, and the index receives only infrequent updates.

datasets.name: Cambridge Cybercrime Centre CrimeBB
datasets.description: The Cambridge Cybercrime Centre shares CrimeBB, a collection of posts scraped from underground cybercrime forums. Related collections cover marketplace contracts, chat channels, and website defacements.
datasets.dataType: Database of forum posts, threads, and user records
datasets.license: Cambridge Cybercrime Centre data sharing agreement
datasets.caveats: Institutional review board (IRB) review and an agreement signed by the researcher's institution are required. Researchers must send the Centre a copy of each paper when it is submitted for peer review. The Centre places significant restrictions on any commercial use of its data.

datasets.name: CyberTweets
datasets.description: CyberTweets is a corpus of tweets annotated for cyber threat relevance and threat type. The repository also includes the web application used by annotators to label the tweets.
datasets.caveats: The tweets predate 2019 and may reference accounts or posts that no longer exist. Any reuse must follow the X platform terms for redistributing content.

datasets.name: Evolution Cryptomarket Structured Dataset
datasets.description: This dataset structures forum and marketplace data from the Evolution dark web market into relational tables. It also provides temporal communication networks built from forum interactions between users.
datasets.size: More than 500,000 forum posts and 80,000 listings
datasets.caveats: Content describes illicit drug and carding trade by pseudonymous users of the market. IRB review is advised before researchers analyze or publish results from these data. Zenodo blocks some automated clients, so researchers may need to download through a browser.

datasets.name: LevelBlue Open Threat Exchange (OTX)
datasets.description: The Open Threat Exchange (OTX), formerly branded AlienVault OTX, is a free community threat intelligence platform. Users share pulses that group IOCs with context about a threat.
datasets.dataType: JSON via DirectConnect API and SDKs
datasets.size: More than 100,000 participants in 140 countries per the provider
datasets.caveats: Pulses are user generated and vary widely in quality, accuracy, and completeness. Researchers should deduplicate indicators and check pulse authorship before any analysis.

datasets.name: Malpedia
datasets.description: Malpedia from Fraunhofer FKIE documents malware families and threat actors with curated report references. Public API endpoints list families, actors, and a bibliography of analysis reports.
datasets.dataType: JSON via REST API and BibTeX
datasets.caveats: Malware samples and some YARA rules require an account in an invite-only trust group. Family and actor naming follows Malpedia conventions that may differ from vendor names.

datasets.name: MISP Default Feeds
datasets.description: The Malware Information Sharing Platform (MISP) project lists public open source intelligence feeds enabled by default. The feeds are distributed in MISP, CSV, and freetext formats for automated import.
datasets.dataType: MISP JSON, CSV, and freetext feeds
datasets.caveats: Each feed has its own provider terms, and at least one listed feed requires a paid license. Researchers should check each source's terms before any redistribution of feed data.

datasets.name: MISP Galaxy
datasets.description: MISP Galaxy provides clusters that describe threat actors, malware families, tools, and related concepts. Clusters include synonyms and relationships that help link intelligence from different vendors.
datasets.caveats: Community contributors maintain the clusters, so actor attributions can conflict with vendor naming. Synonym lists need manual checking before researchers merge entities across sources.

datasets.name: ORKL Threat Report Library
datasets.description: ORKL is a searchable library of threat intelligence reports with extracted text and threat actor links. A public REST API exposes library entries, threat actor records, and library statistics.
datasets.size: 29,534 library entries and 1,945 threat actor entries
datasets.caveats: The web interface is a client-rendered application, so bulk access should use the documented API. Report content remains under the rights of the original publishing vendors.

datasets.name: PEASEC Cybersecurity Dataset
datasets.description: This corpus combines security tweets, blog posts, arXiv security papers, and CVE descriptions. The authors built it to train the CySecBERT domain-adapted language model.
datasets.caveats: The repository shares references only because of data storage and publication restrictions. Researchers must rehydrate tweets and blog text, and some items are no longer available.

datasets.name: Ransomware.live
datasets.description: Ransomware.live tracks victim claims that ransomware groups post on their leak sites. It reports victim metadata, group profiles, and statistics through a website and a public API.
datasets.caveats: Victim claims come from criminal leak sites and are not independently verified. Records name real organizations, so researchers should handle and publish them with care. A separate paid Pro API offers additional features beyond the free public API.

datasets.name: Spamhaus Don't Route Or Peer (DROP)
datasets.description: Spamhaus Don't Route Or Peer (DROP) lists IP ranges that Spamhaus considers too dangerous to route. Separate files cover IPv4 ranges, IPv6 ranges, and autonomous system numbers (ASNs).
datasets.caveats: Spamhaus asks users not to fetch the list automatically more than once per hour. The Extended DROP (EDROP) list merged into DROP on April 10, 2024. Products that use DROP must credit Spamhaus and keep the file copyright text.

datasets.name: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog
datasets.description: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) lists CVEs with confirmed exploitation in the wild. Each entry includes vendor, product, date added, required action, and a known ransomware use flag.
datasets.caveats: The catalog includes only exploitation that CISA has confirmed through its own evidence standards. Absence from KEV does not mean that a vulnerability has never been exploited. A mirror with full commit history is available on GitHub at cisagov/kev-data.

datasets.name: CISA Vulnrichment
datasets.description: CISA acts as an Authorized Data Publisher (ADP) that adds enrichment to selected CVE records. Added fields include Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization (SSVC) decision points, CWE, CVSS, and CPE data.
datasets.dataType: JSON files in a Git repository
datasets.caveats: CISA enriches only a subset of CVEs, so coverage is uneven across vendors and years. The same ADP data also appears inside official CVE Records in the cvelistV5 repository.

datasets.name: CVE List V5 (cvelistV5)
datasets.description: The CVE Program repository holds every CVE Record in the CVE JSON 5 record format. Files update about every seven minutes from the official CVE Services API.
datasets.dataType: JSON files in a Git repository
datasets.caveats: Records mix schema versions 5.0, 5.1, and later, so validate each record against its dataversion field. Legacy CSV, HTML, and XML downloads ended on June 30, 2024 and are no longer updated.

datasets.name: ENISA European Union Vulnerability Database (EUVD)
datasets.description: The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) runs the European Union Vulnerability Database (EUVD) under the NIS2 Directive. It aggregates records from computer security incident response teams (CSIRTs), vendors, and the CVE Program.
datasets.dataType: JSON via REST API and web search
datasets.caveats: The service launched in 2025, so its coverage and data fields are still changing. EUVD identifiers differ from CVE identifiers and need a mapping step before joins.

datasets.name: Exploit Database (Exploit-DB)
datasets.description: Exploit-DB is an archive of public exploits and proof-of-concept code maintained by the company OffSec. The GitLab repository includes the exploit files and a CSV index that lists CVE codes.
datasets.dataType: Source code files and CSV index
datasets.caveats: The archive contains working exploit code, so researchers should handle it inside an isolated environment. Antivirus tools may quarantine some files after download and corrupt a local copy. CVE mappings are missing for many older entries and need manual linking.

datasets.name: FIRST Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS)
datasets.description: The Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) estimates the probability that a CVE is exploited in the next 30 days. Scores and percentiles are published daily for every published CVE through CSV files and an API.
datasets.dataType: Daily CSV files and JSON API
datasets.caveats: Scores produced by different EPSS model versions are not directly comparable over time. EPSS predicts the likelihood of exploitation activity and does not measure impact or severity. Studies of score changes need the archived daily files rather than the current snapshot.

datasets.name: GitHub Advisory Database
datasets.description: GitHub publishes security advisories for open source packages in OSV format under a Creative Commons license. The database separates GitHub-reviewed advisories from unreviewed advisories imported from NVD.
datasets.caveats: Only GitHub-reviewed advisories include curated package names and affected version ranges. Unreviewed advisories are mostly NVD imports that lack package ecosystem data.

datasets.name: Metasploit Framework module metadata
datasets.description: Rapid7 maintains Metasploit modules and a machine-readable metadata file inside the framework repository. The metadata lists module type, CVE references, targets, platforms, and disclosure dates.
datasets.dataType: JSON metadata and Ruby source code
datasets.caveats: Module coverage reflects Rapid7 and community priorities rather than all exploited vulnerabilities. Researchers should analyze the file db/modules_metadata_base.json instead of running any modules.

datasets.name: NVD CVE API 2.0
datasets.description: The National Vulnerability Database (NVD) API returns Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) records with enrichment data. Enrichment adds Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) scores, Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) types, and Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) names. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) also publishes bulk JSON feeds for offline analysis.
datasets.dataType: JSON records via REST API and bulk feeds
datasets.caveats: NVD has carried a growing enrichment backlog since early 2024 because CVE submissions rose sharply. Since April 15, 2026, NIST prioritizes Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), federal, and critical-software CVEs. Unenriched CVEs published before March 1, 2026 are now marked as Not Scheduled for enrichment. A free API key raises the request rate limit compared with anonymous access.

datasets.name: OpenSSF Malicious Packages
datasets.description: The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) collects reports of malicious packages found in open source registries. Reports use the OSV format and cover ecosystems such as npm and PyPI.
datasets.caveats: Records describe real malicious packages, so never install listed versions outside a sandbox. Coverage depends on contributing scanners and community reports rather than full registry audits.

datasets.name: OSV.dev Open Source Vulnerabilities
datasets.description: The OSV.dev service aggregates open source vulnerability records in the shared Open Source Vulnerability (OSV) schema. It covers more than 40 package and operating system ecosystems with affected version ranges.
datasets.dataType: JSON records via Google Cloud Storage zip files and REST API
datasets.size: More than 40 ecosystems from 19 direct sources
datasets.license: Varies by source (CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0, MIT, Apache-2.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0)
datasets.caveats: Each upstream source carries its own license, so attribution rules must be checked per ecosystem. Some records are converted from NVD and inherit its enrichment gaps and delays.

datasets.name: VulZoo
datasets.description: VulZoo integrates 17 vulnerability information sources into one dataset for security research. It links CVEs with exploits, advisories, patches, and threat knowledge bases for downstream tasks.
datasets.dataType: Raw and processed files in a Git repository
datasets.size: 17 sources, 25 GB or more when fully cloned
datasets.caveats: The repository has not received updates since March 2025, so bundled data is dated. Users must run the provided scripts to refresh upstream sources before new analyses.

datasets.name: ARVO
datasets.description: ARVO (Atlas of Reproducible Vulnerabilities) packages OSS-Fuzz vulnerabilities with Docker images, proof-of-concept inputs, and fix commits. Each record includes commands to rebuild the vulnerable and fixed versions of the code.
datasets.dataType: SQLite metadata database and Docker images
datasets.caveats: Docker images need large disk space and a working container runtime. Coverage is limited to open source projects that Google fuzzes through OSS-Fuzz.

datasets.name: Big-Vul
datasets.description: Big-Vul links CVE entries to C and C++ fix commits with code before and after each change. Each row has 21 features including CWE, CVSS subscores, and the developer commit message.
datasets.size: 3,754 vulnerabilities from 348 projects across 91 CWE types
datasets.caveats: Commit-based labels treat every changed function as vulnerable, which adds substantial label noise. The PrimeVul paper documents low label accuracy and duplication in this dataset.

datasets.name: CleanVul
datasets.description: CleanVul uses an LLM scorer with heuristic filters to keep genuine vulnerability-fixing function changes. Each row pairs a function before and after the fix with a confidence score.
datasets.dataType: CSV function pairs with confidence scores
datasets.caveats: Labels depend on LLM judgments, and the reported correctness rates are estimates from the authors. The repository has no stated license, so reuse terms should be confirmed with the authors.

datasets.name: CrossVul
datasets.description: CrossVul pairs vulnerable source files with their patched versions across many programming languages. A supporting dataset adds commit messages from the Git commits that served as security patches.
datasets.dataType: Source files and commit message data in a zip archive
datasets.size: Files in more than 40 languages, about 1.4 GB
datasets.caveats: Labels are assigned at file level, so the specific vulnerable lines are not marked. Zenodo blocks some automated clients, so researchers may need to download through a browser.

datasets.name: CVEfixes
datasets.description: CVEfixes automatically collects CVE records and their fix commits from open source repositories. It stores code before and after each change at file and method level in a relational database.
datasets.size: 11,873 CVEs, 12,107 fix commits, 4,249 projects, 272 CWE types (v1.0.8)
datasets.caveats: Fix commits often include changes unrelated to the vulnerability, which creates noisy function labels. The database file is large and is distributed through Zenodo rather than GitHub.

datasets.name: CyberGym
datasets.description: CyberGym tests artificial intelligence (AI) agents on generating proof-of-concept inputs for real vulnerabilities. Tasks come from open source projects with pre-patch and post-patch builds.
datasets.dataType: Benchmark tasks, binaries, and Docker environments
datasets.caveats: The maintainers warn users to deploy everything locally and never expose it to the internet. Full server data is very large, so storage needs careful planning in advance.

datasets.name: CyberSecEval (Purple Llama)
datasets.description: CyberSecEval from Meta measures whether large language models (LLMs) generate insecure code as coding assistants. It includes autocomplete and instruction tests scored by an insecure code detector.
datasets.dataType: JSON test prompts and evaluation code
datasets.caveats: Only the insecure code tests fit software security research on vulnerable code. Other suites in the repository measure attack compliance and prompt injection instead. Rule-based detection can flag safe code as insecure and inflate reported risk.

datasets.name: Devign
datasets.description: Devign provides manually labeled vulnerability-fixing commits and C functions from large open source projects. The public release covers FFmpeg and QEMU with binary labels for each function.
datasets.dataType: JSON functions and CSV commit labels
datasets.size: FFmpeg and QEMU subsets of a four-project study
datasets.caveats: Only two of the four studied projects are publicly released with function labels. Later studies report duplication and unrealistic class balance that inflate model scores.

datasets.name: DiverseVul
datasets.description: DiverseVul contains vulnerable and non-vulnerable C and C++ functions extracted from security fix commits. It added 295 projects beyond all prior datasets combined at its release.
datasets.size: 18,945 vulnerable and 330,492 non-vulnerable functions from 7,514 commits across 150 CWEs
datasets.caveats: The authors document label noise from commit-based labeling in their own manual analysis. Files are hosted on Google Drive rather than in a versioned research archive.

datasets.name: Draper VDISC
datasets.description: The Draper Vulnerability Detection in Source Code (VDISC) dataset contains C and C++ functions from open source software. Labels come from the findings of three different static analysis tools.
datasets.dataType: HDF5 files with function source and labels
datasets.caveats: Labels come from static analyzer findings rather than confirmed and patched vulnerabilities. Many labeled findings may therefore be false positives that mislead trained models.

datasets.name: MegaVul
datasets.description: MegaVul extracts vulnerable and non-vulnerable functions from CVE fix commits across 28 Git hosting sites. It provides several code representations for training sequence-based and graph-based models.
datasets.size: 17,380 vulnerabilities from 992 repositories across 169 CWE types
datasets.caveats: The GPL-3.0 license places conditions on redistribution of derived datasets and tools. Java data was added after the paper and has different coverage from the C and C++ data.

datasets.name: MoreFixes
datasets.description: MoreFixes mines CVE fix commits through improved repository discovery with the Prospector tool. It extends the CVEfixes schema with many more projects and fix commits.
datasets.caveats: The authors estimate about 4 percent noise from Prospector heuristics in the final dataset. Use the database dump because rebuilding from scratch takes days or weeks. A 2026 release is larger than the version described in the paper.

datasets.name: NIST SARD Juliet Test Suites
datasets.description: The NIST Software Assurance Reference Dataset (SARD) hosts the Juliet test suites for static analysis evaluation. Each test case contains flawed and fixed code mapped to a specific CWE.
datasets.dataType: Source code archives with CWE labels
datasets.size: Juliet C/C++ 1.3 has 64,099 cases, Java 1.3 has 28,881, C# 1.3 has 28,942
datasets.caveats: Juliet code is synthetic and much simpler than real production software. Models trained only on Juliet often fail to generalize to real open source projects.

datasets.name: PrimeVul
datasets.description: PrimeVul is a C and C++ function dataset built with stricter labeling and thorough deduplication. It uses chronological splits and paired vulnerable and patched samples for realistic evaluation.
datasets.dataType: JSONL functions with commit and CVE metadata
datasets.size: About 7,000 vulnerable and 229,000 benign functions covering more than 140 CWEs
datasets.caveats: The paper shows that models scoring well on older datasets perform poorly on PrimeVul. Labels are more accurate than earlier datasets but still come from automated rules.

datasets.name: Project KB (SAP)
datasets.description: Project KB from SAP maps publicly disclosed vulnerabilities in open source Java projects to their fix commits. The knowledge base continues to grow through statements contributed by the community.
datasets.size: 624 vulnerabilities, 205 Java projects, 1,282 fix commits (2019 paper)
datasets.caveats: The dataset centers on Java libraries that SAP products or internal tools use. Current counts exceed the figures reported in the 2019 paper and should be recomputed.

datasets.name: ReposVul
datasets.description: ReposVul is a repository-level vulnerability dataset with untangled patches and inter-procedural context. It includes function, file, and repository level data across four programming languages.
datasets.dataType: JSON records with code and patch context
datasets.size: 6,134 CVEs across 236 CWE types and 1,491 projects
datasets.caveats: Untangling relies on LLM and static analysis filters that can still mislabel code changes. The repository has no stated license, so reuse terms should be confirmed with the authors.

datasets.name: ReVeal (Chromium and Debian)
datasets.description: ReVeal collects vulnerable and fixed C functions from the Chromium and Debian issue trackers. The repository also includes the Devign FFmpeg and QEMU subset used in the same study.
datasets.dataType: Function files with Joern-based processing scripts
datasets.caveats: Data downloads rely on Google Drive links that may change or disappear. The PrimeVul paper reports label noise and duplication across this and similar datasets.

datasets.name: SecurityEval
datasets.description: SecurityEval provides prompts that ask code generation models to complete security-sensitive Python code. Each prompt maps to a CWE and supports static analysis of the generated code.
datasets.caveats: The benchmark is small, so results can vary widely between runs and models. Evaluation depends on static analyzers that can miss or misreport security issues.
